summary: While an answer streams, only that message renders and parses its Markdown; a finished message renders only when something it shows changes. No code change needed; keep config objects stable.
howTo: Nothing to do for the speed-up. Check custom components rendered inside a message (components.MessageBubble with useMessageParts, MessageParts, Markdown, MentionChip, ToolResultBlock, tool renderers, ApprovalEntry, ApprovalCard, ClarificationCard, TurnNotice): they no longer render on every chunk of a later answer. A value that was only refreshed by those renders, such as Date.now() or a relative time computed in render, or state read in render without a subscription (a module variable, a ref, localStorage, an external store without useSyncExternalStore), stays as it was until the message renders again; keep it in state, a subscription or a timer. Effects without a dependency list and render logging run less often. A component that calls useChatContext() itself still renders on every change of the chat context. Apps that change message objects in place should replace them instead (the AI SDK does). Keep config stable to get the speed-up: an app whose component holding the provider renders on every chunk and builds new config objects there (locale, classNames, components, toolLabels, triggers, toolResults, composer, entityDeclarations, entityLinks, toolRenderers, approvalDescription, markdown) renders every message per chunk, as before. Use a module constant, or useMemo for config that depends on state. A change made in place to classNames, components or a toolLabels entry and passed as the same object shows in a finished message only once it renders again; pass a new object. The CHANGELOG lists every difference.
